findings.reason: without a declared injection point the node's two load-bearing cases are unbuildable as written; naming one is a one-clause change and the earlier line-134 finding on this same test was amended for exactly this class of gap.
findings.text: §2's done-when requires the test to run "with the slice size set to one commit" (plan.html:134), and its second case and its third (interruption/resume) case both depend on the window taking several slices, but the section names no knob the test can set: line 124 fixes the size as a property of "this checkout" and the section adds "no public name", so a builder that writes the size as a local constant produces a test that can only ever take one slice and a third case that cannot exercise the resume the section's own negative control reddens; declarable as a module-level constant or a keyword parameter, either of which the test can set

rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the section's diagnostic evidence is at `~/.cache/reckon-velocity-window-check/`, the `~/.cache/<repo>-<topic>/` path the workspace sanctions for logs a later reader needs, and I opened all three files there; no gate log is placed in a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new report value `first_primary_record_file_addition_upper_bound` and the new test path `tests/test_velocity_places_a_run_by_its_record_file.py` name the mechanism, carry no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag, and the section's prose is mechanism, not changelog.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — all three checks hold. The root cause matches the cited evidence: the `TimeoutExpired` logs name the same `git log --first-parent --since… -p -G <ids> origin..head -- crew.json runs/` argv the section describes, and the 2026-09-01 log (`# revision 534f6536e…`, `EXIT=1 seconds=410`) was taken at a head whose base already carries a ledger, so the section is right that the timeout predates §1 rather than being caused by it. Each mechanism can produce its half of the done-when: bounding each git call by ledger-touching-commit slices with the cache's existing `walked` resume keeps every call inside `run_git`'s 180 s bound while carrying the walk across calls, and taking runs out of the `-G` expression via `--diff-filter=A` reduces the search's remaining work without generating a patch. The mechanism runs on the real path: `recover_ledger_clocks` is what `reckon crew velocity …` calls, which is the command both post-merge checks run.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 carries one verdict (a long window's ledger search completes inside its per-call bound and its post-merge checks exit 0); the slicing and the record-file placement are two mechanisms serving that one gate, and the section declares one negative control per mechanism rather than a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-blocks` names `the-ledger-is-one-file-per-run#s4`, and §4 of that plan is the section whose commit deletes `crew.json` (`docs/plans/the-ledger-is-one-file-per-run.html:489`), so the declared relationship points at the node it says it blocks; the plan's other prerequisite, §1, is declared `done` in `plan-section-declarations` and its code is in the tree.
